items.context: Vrooli scenarios target measurable value. Even at this early stage, having a monetization direction helps prioritize features and shape architecture (e.g., multi-tenancy, usage tracking, billing integration). This can be answered independently of round 1 decisions.

options.label: Internal tool — no direct monetization
options.rationale: Value is measured by developer productivity gains. No billing infrastructure needed.

options.label: SaaS with usage-based pricing
options.rationale: Charge per test run, per seat, or per project. Requires usage metering and billing integration.

options.label: Open-source with premium features
options.rationale: Core is free, advanced features (analytics, CI/CD integration, team features) are paid. Wider adoption, slower revenue.

options.label: Bundled with Vrooli platform
options.rationale: Included as a platform capability that increases overall Vrooli value. No standalone pricing.

items.context: Does this idea need a user interface, or is it purely API/CLI-driven? This significantly affects development effort and timeline.

options.label: No UI — API and/or CLI only
options.rationale: Fastest to build. Suitable for developer tools, automation, and agent-consumed capabilities.

options.label: Simple dashboard UI
options.rationale: Read-only or light-interaction UI for viewing results, status, and metrics. Moderate effort.

options.label: Full interactive UI
options.rationale: Rich interface for configuration, execution, and analysis. Highest effort but best UX for non-technical users.

options.label: Embed in web-console
options.rationale: Add capabilities to the existing Vrooli web console rather than a standalone UI. Leverages existing frontend infrastructure.

items.context: If this idea involves executing user-provided code or tests, security isolation is critical. Vrooli's agent-manager already has sandbox capabilities that could be leveraged.

options.label: No special isolation — trusted internal execution
options.rationale: Runs only trusted code within the Vrooli server. Simplest architecture.

options.label: Sandboxed execution via agent-manager
options.rationale: Leverage existing sandbox infrastructure for untrusted code/test execution. Proven isolation model.

options.label: Container-based isolation
options.rationale: Each execution runs in its own container. Heavier but maximum isolation.

items.context: The test-genie scenario already provides AI-assisted test generation. Regardless of what this new idea is, we need to decide how it relates to test-genie to avoid duplication and maximize synergy.

options.label: Completely independent — different domain
options.rationale: This idea has nothing to do with test generation. No overlap concern.

options.label: Complementary — different capability, same ecosystem
options.rationale: Both live in the testing space but address different problems. Could share data or call each other's APIs.

options.label: Replacement — supersedes test-genie
options.rationale: This idea is a better version of what test-genie does. test-genie would be deprecated.

options.label: Extension — builds on top of test-genie
options.rationale: Uses test-genie as a dependency/building block. Adds capabilities that test-genie doesn't have.

Rounds 2-4 can be answered in parallel or deferred.
